events.title: Exact semantic-survival witness discovery is SAT-hard in the general circuit scope
statement: For Boolean circuit/B2 DAG C and partial assignment rho, SURVIVE(C,rho) means C|rho is nonconstant.
SURVIVE is in NP because two completions alpha,beta with different outputs form a polynomially verifiable witness.
SAT reduces linearly: F(x) maps to C_F(z,x)=z AND F(x) with empty rho; F is satisfiable iff C_F is nonconstant.
Therefore general residual nonconstancy is NP-complete and residual constancy is coNP-complete.
claim_boundary: This does not prove hardness for the exact Sokolov source-matched restriction relation.
This does not prove a superpolynomial lower bound for every restricted macro language.

events.title: Constructive bi-witness macro language isolated; one-witness completeness fails and witness-frontier width becomes the next exact resource
statement: Accepted AND candidates can inherit a positive witness without semantic search when child positive witnesses are compatible on overlap.
All explicit operand pairs in state size V are enumerable in O(V^2), so accepted-step discovery is polynomial in explicit state size.
One retained positive witness per function is not compositionally complete: a=x OR y and b=x OR NOT y can carry incompatible retained positive witnesses although a AND b is nonconstant.
The next resource is witness-frontier width Omega(S), the maximum retained constructive positive-witness count per represented function.

active_front.name: AKINATOR-RSPC-S2
active_front.question: Can a source-matched constructive macro language retain only polynomially many survival witnesses in original input length N while guaranteeing a deterministic no-backtracking admissible step at every nonterminal target state?
forbidden_shortcuts: polynomial in cache size without input-relative accounting
provider CI promoted to NP-completeness theorem
